warning: SYNTHETIC EVIDENCE ONLY. These numbers measure agreement between the engine and the claim contract it implements. They are not a measurement of real-world performance and must not be reported as one.

corruption_catalogue.name: conflict_summary_detail
corruption_catalogue.rationale: the daily summary and the interval detail disagree, the signature of two different syncs or two different days being combined

corruption_catalogue.name: delay_sync
corruption_catalogue.rationale: the last successful sync finished before the window ended, so part of the window has not reached the server yet

corruption_catalogue.name: destabilize_baseline
corruption_catalogue.rationale: the baseline swings so widely that no change can be distinguished from ordinary day-to-day variation

corruption_catalogue.name: drop_contiguous
corruption_catalogue.rationale: a contiguous block of the window is missing, as happens when a device is charged mid-window; wear time is reduced consistently with the hole

corruption_catalogue.name: drop_random
corruption_catalogue.rationale: samples are missing at random across the window, as happens with an unreliable sync; the summary aggregates survive while the detail thins out

corruption_catalogue.name: drop_timezone
corruption_catalogue.rationale: the subject's timezone is missing or invalid, so a calendar-day window cannot be placed; this is the quiet source of off-by-one-day insights

corruption_catalogue.name: dropout_flags
corruption_catalogue.rationale: the pipeline reports sensor dropout or device removal across part of the window

corruption_catalogue.name: duplicate_samples
corruption_catalogue.rationale: samples are duplicated by a retried sync. The engine must deduplicate and still decide; abstaining here would be over-abstention, so this stays SUPPORTABLE

corruption_catalogue.name: flatline
corruption_catalogue.rationale: the sensor sticks and repeats one value; a stuck reading looks like admirably steady physiology unless it is checked for

corruption_catalogue.name: implausible_spike
corruption_catalogue.rationale: impossible values appear in the required signal, which indicates a sensor or pipeline fault rather than a physiological event

corruption_catalogue.name: motion_artifact
corruption_catalogue.rationale: optical measurements are contaminated by movement, the dominant failure mode for wrist PPG; values survive but are not trustworthy

corruption_catalogue.name: shift_baseline
corruption_catalogue.rationale: the baseline contains a level shift, so its mean describes neither the earlier nor the later period

corruption_catalogue.name: shift_day_boundary
corruption_catalogue.rationale: the window is placed a few hours off, as happens after travel or a DST change, so the evidence describes a different day than the claim

corruption_catalogue.name: shorten_wear
corruption_catalogue.rationale: the device was worn for much less of the window than the claim requires

corruption_catalogue.name: shuffle_order
corruption_catalogue.rationale: samples arrive out of chronological order. The engine must sort and still decide; this stays SUPPORTABLE for the same reason as duplication

corruption_catalogue.name: stale_data
corruption_catalogue.rationale: the whole evidence bundle is old: evaluation happens long after the newest measurement and the last sync

corruption_catalogue.name: truncate_baseline
corruption_catalogue.rationale: the personal baseline is too short to say what is normal for this person, the situation every new user is in

baselines_not_implemented.B4_hybrid_calibrated: requires public datasets and a calibration split
